solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Your health the worst: drink!

parts.note: the bottom is the lowest, worst position, as in bottom of the class
to sup is to drink, in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A grim toast: here's to your health, the worst is over, so drink up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink!' reads as the toast's command, but it only supplies SUP; the definition is the opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts spoken when raising glasses, wishing well-being to the company.

clue.text: Vehicle experiencing programming malfunction?

definitions.meaning: software with faults, called bugs, is said to be full of them

explanation.surface: A car whose software is glitching.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram or small carriage is a vehicle; code with many errors is riddled with faults.

clue.text: Hunger matters around mealtime, starter polished off before one

indicators.note: the matters word goes around the meal-and-one pieces

parts.note: themes are matters or subjects under discussion

indicators.note: before puts the trimmed meal ahead of the one
the starter, the first letter of the mealtime, is eaten up and removed

parts.note: lunch is a mealtime
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dinner scene: someone has eaten their starter and is hungry before one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polished off' looks like eating up a first course; it means the first letter is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase means a sudden craving for snacks, a kind of appetite.

clue.text: In action working, he got to work

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: to work means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Busy and active: he got to his job on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone always busy and moving about is active, never resting.

clue.text: Key establishment selling out-of-this-world drinks?

definitions.meaning: the long bar at the bottom of a keyboard
a pub in outer space would sell drinks literally out of this world

explanation.surface: A bar whose cocktails are heavenly holds the key to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-this-world' usually means superb; here it means beyond Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The wide keyboard key types a gap, and a pub in orbit would also earn the name.

clue.text: Englishman abroad, one remains reduced to a pulp

parts.note: Pom is Australian and New Zealand slang for an English person
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: An Englishman overseas stays put while someone else is beaten to a pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the crushed pulp left after pressing apples or grapes for juice.

clue.text: Confirmation is academic, being empty?

indicators.note: the academic is being empty, so the nothing sits within the professor's letters

parts.note: prof is short for professor, a university academic
O is a zero, an empty ring with nothing inside

explanation.surface: A sly dig at scholars: is a confirmation merely academic, a hollow formality?
explanation.walkthrough: 'academic' looks like an adjective meaning theoretical; it is the noun, a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that settles a matter, such as a receipt or a test result, confirms it.

clue.text: Predator managed to gatecrash a joint from the basement?

indicators.note: to gatecrash is to push in uninvited, so managed enters the other letters
in a down clue, read from the basement means read upwards, so the letters are backwards

parts.note: the hip is a joint
to run something is to manage it, so managed gives ran

explanation.surface: An intruder manages to crash a party at a joint, sneaking in from the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the basement' turns A plus the joint upwards, giving PIHA, and 'to gatecrash' sends the managed word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American fish with razor teeth that hunts other animals.

clue.text: Eye relative up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a relative who is up and about.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry an eyeball is a round sphere, a literary name for the eye.

clue.text: Fling in cash for sybarite

indicators.note: in places the dance inside the cash

parts.note: a fiver is a five-pound note, a sum of cash in Britain
a reel is a lively dance, like the Highland fling

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker has a fling with money in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' suggests an affair; here it is a dance, the reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite indulges in luxury and pleasure, like someone with an indulgent lifestyle.

clue.text: Patron supposed to be heard?

indicators.note: the clue asks for the word as spoken, so the sound of guessed is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: to suppose is to guess, so supposed gives guessed

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person is supposed to be listened to as a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a hotel or restaurant is a customer staying or dining there, a visitor being served.

clue.text: Good, fertile housing market initially in brief dip

indicators.note: housing means the fertile word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: arable land is fertile, fit for growing crops

indicators.note: in places the market's first letter within the shortened dip
brief means cut short, so the word dip loses its final letter

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim, a dip

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of market is taken

explanation.surface: A farming report: fertile land is supporting the property market despite a short downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' removes the dip's last letter; 'in' puts M within what is left, making DMI, which 'housing' places inside the fertile word.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable conduct is worthy, deserving praise, which is what good means here.

clue.text: An imperative in confidentiality agreement? Who knows?

definitions.meaning: read as an order, the phrase forbids ever revealing a secret, the core of a non-disclosure deal
an expression of uncertainty, saying the outcome is impossible to predict

explanation.surface: A lawyer pores over a non-disclosure agreement and shrugs about what it really demands.
explanation.walkthrough: The common saying meaning 'it's unpredictable' is reread literally as a command never to tell anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses that nobody can be sure, matching the shrug of a rhetorical question about knowledge.

clue.text: Radioactive element beginning to escape in minutes, I suspect

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of escape
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A physicist fears radioactive material will start leaking within minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic element, number 99, is radioactive, named after a famous physicist.

clue.text: Cult said to be in pieces

definitions.note: an adjective meaning divided into parts, here the parts of an economy

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult or faction
oral means spoken, said rather than written

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a cult has fallen apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound signal; here it simply means spoken, giving ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectoral describes something split into separate divisions or segments, as an economy is into industries.

clue.text: Cheat on bouncer, odd character

parts.note: to screw someone is slang for cheating or swindling them
a ball bounces

explanation.surface: Cheating on a nightclub doorman would make someone a strange type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman; it is simply something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric, unpredictable person is a crazy oddball.

clue.text: Driving aid positioned in front of reversing vehicle

indicators.note: in front of places the positioned word before the turned vehicle

parts.note: something sat on a shelf is positioned there

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the vehicle's letters backwards

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A gadget mounted on the dashboard, placed ahead of a driver backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing vehicle' suggests a car backing up, but it turns VAN into NAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation device guides motorists, helping them find their route.

clue.text: Savage not to be trusted after a scalping?

indicators.note: scalping removes the top, so the first letter is taken off

parts.note: truthless means lacking truth, so unreliable

explanation.surface: A brutal warrior, never to be trusted after scalping victims.
explanation.definitionFit: A savage attack is merciless, showing no pity at all.

clue.text: Fruit is getting watered, presumably?

indicators.note: the word is is getting rain all around it, so it sits inside

parts.note: something watered has presumably had rain fall on it

explanation.surface: A wry thought on dried grapes: once the fruit is watered, does it plump up again?
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting watered' pictures the word 'is' being rained on all round. The joke is that this dried fruit is anything but watered.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar fruit used in baking.

clue.text: Swell occupying fifth apartment?

parts.note: in means occupying, living inside
flat is British for an apartment, and the fifth one in a block would be lettered E

explanation.surface: A tenant living in the fifth flat of a block.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'in flat E': the flats are lettered A to E, so the fifth is E.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand, to grow bigger as a balloon does.

clue.text: Comedian absolutely right to defend further comment

indicators.note: to defend is to surround protectively, so absolutely encloses the further comment

parts.note: quite can mean absolutely, completely
PS, postscript, is a further comment added to a letter

explanation.surface: A comic is absolutely entitled to stand by a follow-up remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A quipster trades in witty remarks, the stock of anyone who makes people laugh.

clue.text: Writer and poet ultimately wanting jewellery

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool

indicators.note: ultimately wanting means the last letter is missing

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A writer and a poet both in the end desire jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like desiring; here it means lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging ornament worn on a chain around the neck is a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Beer bottles container for French region

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so beer encloses the container

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a sac is a pouch, a container in a body

explanation.surface: Beer bottled in a container from a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a plural noun; it is the verb, to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an area of north-eastern France on the German border, famous for wine.

clue.text: After gallivanting, in with flush, high card too much to expect?

indicators.note: gallivanting means roaming about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the king is a high card in a pack

explanation.surface: A poker player, having gone out on the town, hopes for a flush and a high card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After gallivanting' shuffles the three words into WISHFULTHIN; the card is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoping for an outcome that reality is unlikely to deliver is daydreaming, expecting more than is reasonable.

clue.text: Snapper dropping camera went to mender, finally

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A photographer dropped a camera and took it to the repairer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapper' suggests a photographer, fitting the camera; it is a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator, with its snapping jaws, is a creature that bites hard.

clue.text: Put out sepulchre that's cut in stone

indicators.note: in places the shortened tomb inside the stone

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone

indicators.note: cut means the word for sepulchre loses its last letter

parts.note: a sepulchre is a tomb, a grave

explanation.surface: Annoy someone with a tomb carved into the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like a verb meaning extinguish; here it means irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out is annoyed, so to put out is to irritate or exasperate.

clue.text: Being worshipped, boxer, say, lifted up

indicators.note: lifted up means in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, an example

explanation.surface: A boxer being worshipped after being lifted up in victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter; it is a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity is a being worshipped as divine.

clue.text: Star featuring in musical is terrific

indicators.note: featuring in signals the answer appears within the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A rave review: the star appearing in this musical is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity on the top tier of fame belongs to the elite group of performers.

clue.text: Skirt on back of horizontal shelf

indicators.note: on means the skirt word follows the letter from horizontal
back of means the last letter of horizontal

parts.note: to skirt is to go along the edge of something

explanation.surface: A skirt laid flat on the back of a horizontal shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a garment; here it is the border of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow flat projection from a wall or cliff forms a shelf.

clue.text: State failed doctor in Irish country

indicators.note: failed suggests something broken, so the letters of State are rearranged
in places the doctor inside the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A failed state sees a doctor sent into an Irish country practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the definition; it is the anagram fodder, rearranged by 'failed'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an independent nation in Southeast Asia, sharing an island with Indonesia.
